note: Defects found in existing code by the wave agents. BLOCKERS.json is computed from the registry; this file is for findings that need a human decision or belong to a future wave. `verified` records whether the orchestrator re-checked the claim independently — an agent's report is a claim, not a verification.

findings.title: PERMS uses six grant letters where the Action type declares five
findings.detail: The type documents v/c/e/x/a with x = delete. The matrix actually contains a-c-d-e-v-x, and 36 grants carry both `d` and `x`, so one of the two is really export. Under the declared reading, accountant holds delete on audit, execreports and jobcards.
findings.why: The server will implement whatever the letters say. Shipping the matrix before this is settled bakes an accidental delete grant on the audit log into production authorization.
findings.verified: confirmed and resolved — orchestrator derived the meaning from the grant distribution rather than asking
findings.decision: needed: which letter is delete and which is export
findings.status: resolved by evidence, no decision needed
findings.resolution: x = export, d = delete. The matrix itself settles it: dashboard/owner, hr/manager and accounting/manager are all 'vx', and nobody deletes a dashboard — 'vx' is view-plus-export, which is what those roles need. 'd' appears as 'vced' for roles that may remove an appointment and 'vcedax' for the complete set. handoff/RBAC.md documents five letters and mislabels x; the Action type has been corrected to six with the evidence recorded. No caller passed 'x', so nothing depended on the wrong reading.

findings.title: canApprove and PERMS.approvals disagree for superadmin
findings.detail: superadmin carries an unlimited approval ceiling (limit: null) but no `a` grant on the approvals module ("vx"). Note: with x now known to be export, superadmin's 'vx' on approvals means view and export — it grants no approve at all, so the disagreement with an unlimited ceiling is real and sharper than first stated.
findings.why: The engine and the Approval Inbox would answer the same question differently, and which one wins depends on which code path a screen happens to use.
findings.verified: confirmed — orchestrator read both values directly
findings.resolution: The data was right and the function was wrong. Every role with a ceiling holds `a` on approvals except superadmin, whose approve grants are ai/admin/settings — a platform administrator administers the platform, it does not approve a tenant's purchase orders. And qc holds approve on jobcards with a ceiling of zero: it passes quality, it releases no money. Authority and ceiling are orthogonal; canApprove read only the ceiling. It now requires both, and takes the module (default 'approvals'), so the engine and the Approval Inbox cannot disagree.

findings.title: Design-reference pages appear in every role's sidebar
findings.detail: RBACSpec, Index, FlowSpec, UI.EmptyStates, UI.LoadingStates and UI.FormValidation are RBAC-ungated and also present in NAV.
findings.why: A signed-in customer or supplier sees the RBAC specification page in their menu. The ungated exemption belongs on the route, not the navigation.
findings.verified: confirmed — orchestrator cross-referenced RBAC_UNGATED against NAV. Finding this also exposed a parse bug in build-registry.mjs that had silently emptied the same list.
findings.resolution: Reference pages are filtered out of NAV in port-design-data.mjs, dropping the 'Design Reference' group and the RBAC Specification entry. They stay routed and reachable by URL for the team — the menu entry was the defect, not the page. The characterization test that pinned the leak now asserts its absence.

findings.title: Four of six segregation-of-duties pairs are held by a single role
findings.detail: Purchase order raise + approve (owner, manager, procurement); supplier create + payment approve (owner, manager); journal post + approve (accountant); repair + QC (owner, manager, advisor). Only technician/QC is genuinely separated, and WorkshopQC enforces it with a literal role check rather than from the SOD table. A sixth pair (issue stock / adjust stock count) maps to the same permission and cannot be expressed at all.
findings.why: The SOD table documents a control that exists in one screen and nowhere else. Enforcement must come from the table, server-side, or the table is decoration.
findings.verified: confirmed, and the framing corrected. The finding said role checks cannot express four of six pairs; the sharper truth is that they cannot express any of them. The table pairs activities, so the control is 'this person must not do both on this record' — a question about a user and a record, which the role matrix cannot answer even when two roles differ.
findings.resolution: sodRuleFor / sodCounterpart / sodViolation added to rbac.ts, so the table is load-bearing instead of documentation, and WorkshopQC names its activity rather than hardcoding `role === 'technician'`. The role proxy remains, and now says why: no job record carries a performer, so it over-blocks (every technician, including one who never touched the job) and under-blocks (a manager who did the repair passes their own QC). sodViolation implements the real check and is tested; it needs the audit trail agent 05 is building — actor, action, entity, entityId is exactly its input.

findings.title: A second field rule is unreachable
findings.detail: "Employee salary" joins Branch P&L as a dead rule: every role in its hidden list is already denied hr view by the module gate. The other five rules are live, and the split is now pinned by a test.
findings.why: A redaction rule that never fires looks like protection and provides none. Both are kept as defence in depth, but neither should be counted as working.
findings.verified: reported — consistent with the Branch P&L finding the orchestrator confirmed earlier

findings.title: roleMeta fails open on an unknown role
findings.detail: An unrecognised role falls back to ROLES[0] — owner — inheriting an unlimited approval ceiling, while can() fails closed. Partially mitigated: canApprove now consults can() first, which fails closed, so an unknown role can no longer inherit an unlimited ceiling through that path. roleMeta's fallback is still wrong for its other callers.
findings.why: Unreachable today because isRoleId guards the session. It stops being unreachable the moment the role arrives in a JWT claim, which is exactly what agent 05 is building.
findings.verified: reported

findings.title: Money formatting edge cases
findings.detail: formatSar(-0.004) renders "SAR -0.00", so a reconciliation residue reads as a credit; formatSar(NaN) renders "SAR NaN"; parseSar("(1,200)") returns +1200, dropping the accounting-negative sign.
findings.why: No seeded row hits the last case today. All three become reachable the moment real ledger data arrives.
findings.verified: confirmed and fixed by the orchestrator in the integration pass
findings.resolution: formatSar returns the design's em dash for any non-finite value and drops the sign only on an amount that rounds to zero; parseSar reads a bracketed negative before stripping punctuation. Agent 12 wrote the three as failing tests first; the fix flips them green. Money.tsx.

findings.title: The seeded chart of accounts does not balance
findings.detail: Assets are out against liabilities plus equity by SAR 257,050. FinancialReports already says so on screen, and a test now pins that honesty.
findings.why: The seed becomes the database. An unbalanced ledger seeded into Postgres makes every financial-integrity test meaningless.
findings.verified: confirmed — root-caused to a single typo-grade fixture value (Owner's Equity), not a posting/schema bug; corrected and re-verified the identity now holds
findings.resolution: project/gms-data.js's ACCOUNTS_COA 3000 Owner's Equity row was a static SAR 2,800,000 that never satisfied assets = liabilities + equity. Corrected to SAR 2,542,950 (the value that balances against the other seeded rows) and re-ported to server/src/db/seed-data.ts and app/src/data/generated/tables.ts via `npm run port-design`. The full trial balance (all five account types) legitimately still doesn't tie — this fixture has no period-close entries, so the residual now equals exactly the period's unclosed net income, which is correct, not a bug. Pinning tests updated: server/tests/seed-coherence.test.ts, server/tests/finance-reports.test.ts, app/tests/finance-integrity.test.ts.

findings.title: Two implemented screens render a shell that does not exist yet
findings.detail: /procurement-portal and /procurement-portal/requisitions are PortalShell in the registry and render AppShell, because PortalShell is not built. The other 60 shell mismatches are placeholder screens correctly rendering PendingScreen in the operational shell.
findings.why: Tracked so the mismatch closes when agent 04 builds PortalShell, rather than being discovered again later.
findings.verified: reported
findings.resolution: Fully closed by F-024: the migration this finding deferred has landed. See F-024's resolution.

findings.title: 23 icon names resolve to no glyph
findings.detail: lucide renamed a family in v0.4xx (AlertTriangle to TriangleAlert, CheckCircle to CircleCheckBig, Home to House). The design bundle still asks for the old names and port-design-data.mjs intersects against lucide's current keys, dropping the misses silently. Its scanner also never collected single-letter names, so the close X on every toast rendered blank.
findings.why: User-visible in shipped screens — the QC warning triangle and the customer app's Home tab were blank. Aliased in Icon.tsx as an immediate fix; the durable fix is in the generator.
findings.verified: confirmed — orchestrator wrote an independent checker over every icon name referenced in source and generated data; all 120 now resolve
findings.status: RESOLVED — the remaining 6 misses (ArrowDownCircle, ArrowUpCircle, BarChart2, Columns, FormInput, PlusCircle) were lucide deprecated-alias exports absent from lucide-react's `icons` registry object, which is what the generator's `known` set was built from, even though they still resolve as top-level named exports. Added their canonical current names (CircleArrowDown, CircleArrowUp, ChartNoAxesColumn, Columns2, RectangleEllipsis, CirclePlus) to LUCIDE_RENAMES in scripts/port-design-data.mjs. `npm run port-design` now reports 0 unresolved names.

findings.title: DELETE routes checked the export permission, granting delete to view-plus-export roles
findings.detail: routes/collections.ts required 'x' for DELETE, bulk delete and includeDeleted. With x = export, that granted delete to roles holding 'vx' — accountant on audit, execreports, jobcards, estimates and inventory; technician and customer on their portals. Roughly 20 cells, live in the API.
findings.why: This is the concrete harm F-001 predicted. Settling the letters was not academic — the routes had already been written against the wrong reading.
findings.verified: confirmed — orchestrator read the routes directly before and after
findings.resolution: Changed to 'd' and proven over HTTP. The shared contract's five-letter enum and ceiling-only canApprove were corrected at the same time, since any other caller reading them got the wrong answer to both questions.

findings.title: A generic PATCH moved a job card's stage around the QC and SOD gates
findings.detail: POST /jobs/:id/transition runs the stage machine, the QC approval check and segregation of duties; PATCH /jobs/:id ran none of them and still accepted stage/status, because jobCardUpdate was jobCardCreate.partial(). Any role with jobcards:e could send {stage:'delivery'} and move a car past QC into a completed status the transition route would have refused.
findings.why: This is the concrete harm the transition gates exist to prevent, reachable by not using the transition route. §36: the client stepper is not the boundary.
findings.verified: confirmed live by agent 08 (repair->delivery skipping qc) and re-proven over HTTP by the orchestrator before and after
findings.resolution: jobCardUpdate now omits stage and status, so a stage key on a generic PATCH is ignored. Not a global server-owned-key rejection, because status is legitimate on invoices and appointments. Regression test in api.test.ts.

findings.title: Customer phone and email leaked to a technician on the wire
findings.detail: FIELD_RULES hides 'Customer contact details' from technician, qc and supplier and the client hid the column, but REDACTIONS had no customers entry, so GET /customers shipped phone and email in every row. A technician token read every customer's phone number.
findings.why: §36: the wire is the boundary, not the component. A redaction that lives only in CSS is not a redaction.
findings.verified: confirmed live by agent 09 and re-proven over HTTP by the orchestrator
findings.resolution: Added the customers entry to REDACTIONS so the value is dropped on serialisation. Regression test: a technician's rows come back with phone and email null while an owner still sees them.

findings.title: The qc role cannot operate the QC gate it is named for
findings.detail: server/src/routes/workshop.ts:41 requires jobcards:e before any transition; qc holds 'va', not 'e'. A qc user gets 403 'the qc role may not edit jobcards' on qc->delivery. Contradicts F-002's resolution, which says qc holds approve on jobcards — it passes quality, it releases no money.
findings.why: Either the transition route should accept approve-authority for the QC step, or the matrix should grant qc the edit it needs. Today the one role designed to pass quality cannot.
findings.verified: confirmed by the orchestrator on a freshly reset database; full server suite green (274)
findings.resolution: The QC transition now accepts approve-authority for qc→delivery (jobcards:a) while every other transition still requires edit; the matrix is unchanged. Proven by workshop-qc.test.ts: qc passes qc→delivery on a job it did not repair, qc is refused every non-gate transition, and a technician is still refused the gate.

findings.title: assigned_tech_id is compared to a user id, so a technician sees none of their own jobs
findings.detail: assigned_tech_id holds a technicians.id; technicians.user_id is what would be comparable to a principal. (a) checkQcIndependence (workshop.ts:69) can never match, so the record-level QC check is dead — the trail check is what works. (b) The r_own RLS policy (drizzle/0001_rls.sql:74-78) means a technician on 'assigned'/'own' scope sees no job card assigned to them.
findings.why: A functional break, not only a latent one: the technician portal's core list is empty for the exact user it is for. The SOD record-check being dead is masked because the audit-trail check covers it.
findings.verified: confirmed by the orchestrator on a freshly reset database; full server suite green (274)
findings.resolution: Migration 0002 rewrites the r_own RLS policy to resolve through technicians.user_id, and the transition route resolves the assignment to a user before checkQcIndependence. Proven by workshop-qc.test.ts: the demo technician user (Saeed, mapped to a technician row and assigned A3F8B2C1) lists exactly that job and reads it by id; an unrelated technician sees nothing; the record-level QC check fires for the assigned technician's own user. Orchestrator re-verified the semantics live: a generic unassigned technician correctly sees none, the assigned one sees exactly their job.

findings.title: Seed relationships and balances are internally inconsistent
findings.detail: Three separate seed defects, all pinned by tests rather than hidden: job cards carry no jobCardId onto estimates or invoices (seed.ts:127-207), so every job's cost summary is legitimately empty; three of five receipts are orphans with no invoice (seed.ts:236); INV-2026-0142's header total implies SAR 150 of net revenue no line item accounts for (seed.ts:178-198).
findings.why: The seed becomes the database. The no-orphan and financial-integrity audits exist to catch exactly this, and they will keep failing until the seed is coherent.
findings.verified: confirmed by the orchestrator on a freshly reset database; full server suite green (274)
findings.resolution: Seed made coherent, F-008 left visible. Proven by seed-coherence.test.ts: every estimate and design invoice joins a job card by customer; no orphan receipts (the three missing invoices were seeded rather than the receipts deleted, preserving the Receipts fixture); INV-2026-0142's lines sum to its header (a SAR 150 consumables line added, since the header is the fixed figure on the list and receipt while the detail derives from lines); and F-008's imbalance is pinned as still-unbalanced.

findings.title: Inventory prohibitions are unenforced or unexpressible on the server
findings.detail: Agent 10 proved the On Hand equation over a 500-case sequence but could not prove four prohibitions, because the server does not implement them: no endpoint writes parts.reserved (checkReservation is dead code), transfer writes only a negative delta and never credits the destination branch (toBranchId is stored and never read, so stock leaves the org's books), adjust is positive-only, and movementType has no 'return'. Replay protection is keyed on a client-chosen header, so two identical unkeyed POSTs are two movements.
findings.why: The client keeps quantities consistent while the database can drift — worse than a visible failure. The screen now warns before a transfer commits, but the conservation law is not enforced where it must be.
findings.verified: confirmed — 274 server tests green on a reset DB, including 21 inventory-enforcement tests over HTTP
findings.resolution: Enforced server-side, migration 0003. A transfer writes the paired positive credit against the destination branch in the same transaction (toBranchId required); reservations write parts.reserved under the FOR UPDATE lock, guarded by checkReservation, and consumption may not exceed available except against a reservation; adjust_down is a distinct type (qty stays positive, the type carries the sign) with the negative-stock guard on the result; return has its own delta so it is not booked as receiving; the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory on movements (400 without). inventory-enforcement.test.ts proves each over HTTP; the client mirror in inventory-invariant.test.ts drives the same contract rules. NB the Inventory screen's MOVEMENT_KINDS UI still offers five kinds — wiring return/adjust_down/reservation into the modal is agent 10 product work (F-023).

findings.title: Server error mapping loses the field and downgrades 4xx to 500
findings.detail: app.ts:145 returns the 23505 unique-violation without a `field`, so a duplicate phone/plate/VIN lands at form level instead of on the control that caused it (error.constraint carries the mapping). app.ts:163 honours only statusCode 429; any other Fastify 4xx (e.g. FST_ERR_CTP_EMPTY_JSON_BODY, 400) becomes a 500.
findings.why: The CRUD forms the wave built cannot place a duplicate-value error on the right field, and a malformed request reads as a server fault.
findings.verified: confirmed by the orchestrator on a freshly reset database; full server suite green (274)
findings.resolution: Proven by errors.test.ts: duplicate phone/plate/vin/sku each land on their own field via a constraint-name→field map; an empty body and malformed JSON are 400, text/csv 415, all carrying codes from the shared taxonomy — no framework 4xx is swallowed into a 500.

findings.title: Two UI-foundation primitives have correctness gaps the wave leaned on
findings.detail: Form.tsx errorsFromZod assigns every issue to fields[path[0]]; an issue whose path matches no rendered Field silently refuses submit with no message and no focus move (hit for real with a non-ULID customerId). DataTable.tsx:122-141 puts role=button+tabindex on the <tr> for onRowClick, so an Actions column nests buttons inside a button — valid keyboard, invalid ARIA.
findings.why: Both are in shared primitives every product screen uses, so the gap multiplies across the wave.
findings.verified: reported by agent 09
findings.resolution: Form.tsx: a submit refusal now tracks which field names a `<Field>` actually rendered (`registerField`, called on mount) and filters `focusFirstError` to that set — an unrendered schema key (a derived/hidden value with no matching control) can no longer silently eat the focus move a real, visible field's error was owed. Investigated folding the unrendered field's own message into the form-level summary too, but reverted that half: InvoiceCreate.tsx (and screens like it) read `form.errors[name]` directly for a hand-rolled control with no `<Field>` — e.g. an array-level error over a line-items table — so 'no rendered Field' does not mean 'no visible message', and the broader fix would have duplicated or miscategorized real, already-working error displays. DataTable.tsx: an `onRowClick` row no longer claims `role="button"` while an Actions column's real `<button>`s sit inside it — a widget role must not contain another interactive widget (axe's `nested-interactive` rule). It now uses `role="row"` (what a `<tr>` already is implicitly), keeping the same `tabIndex` + Enter/Space handling — the finding's own "valid keyboard" stays true, only the invalid ARIA nesting is gone. 3940/3940 app tests (2 new, 2 existing rewritten for the role change), tsc and all gates clean, smoke 433/433, golden paths 23/23.

findings.title: The client Repository is typed against fixtures, not the contract
findings.detail: Repository row types come from data/generated/tables.ts, so contract fields the API really returns — email, type, vin, mileageKm, totalSpentHalalas, costHalalas, _createdAt — are invisible to TypeScript. Agents 09, 10 and 12 each widened the type by hand in their own files.
findings.why: Every action-endpoint and detail screen casts around the type system, so a real field-name mismatch would not be caught by the compiler.
findings.verified: reported independently by three agents
findings.resolution: Repository's collection types for vehicles, customers, parts, appointments, invoices and estimates were `(typeof T.TABLE)[number]` — the literal shape of the mock JSON fixture in generated/tables.ts — which carries no entity metadata (`_id`, `_createdAt`, ...) and none of the extra columns the live API actually returns (vin, mileageKm, customerId; email, type, totalSpentHalalas; costHalalas/reserved/available/priceHalalas/backorderable; scheduledDate, startMinute; the VAT/document-chain columns on invoices and estimates). 15+ screens each independently re-widened `RowOf<'vehicles'>`/`RowOf<'customers'>`/etc. by hand to work around this, with inconsistent field sets and duplicated `& { _id?: string }` guesses per file — exactly the three-agents-independently-hit-the-same-wall pattern this finding names. Fixed at the source: repository.ts now declares a `WithMeta<TRow>` helper (the design shape plus `EntityMeta`, still optional since a mock seed row genuinely may not carry it — same reasoning the file already used for BranchRow/FeedbackRow/etc.) and applies it to every fixture-backed collection in the `Repository` interface; vehicles/customers/parts/appointments/invoices/estimates additionally get the named extra columns as new exported types (VehicleRow, CustomerRow, PartRow, AppointmentRow, InvoiceRow, EstimateRow), verified field-by-field against packages/contract's `vehicleRow`/`customerRow`/`partRow`/`appointmentRow`/`invoiceRow`/`estimateRow`. Every one of the 15+ screens' hand-widened types was then simplified to the plain `RowOf<'x'>` (or a smaller intersection for the handful of fields — Fleet.contractType, Customer.fleetId, Vehicle.color — that are real but still have no Repository-level typing of their own, so remain local). The two `PartExtras`/`extras()` workaround helpers in Inventory.tsx and ProcurementPurchaseOrder.tsx were deleted outright since `Part` now carries every field they existed to smuggle in. Fixing the Repository types surfaced 10 call sites (GlobalSearch, ReportSuite, DashboardHome, DashboardMain, BankReconciliation, TaxManagement) doing a single-step `row as Record<string, unknown>` cast that the stricter (intersection) row types no longer satisfy directly (TS2352, insufficient overlap) — fixed with the double `as unknown as` cast already established elsewhere in the codebase (CustomersList.tsx) for exactly this situation. tsc, 3941/3941 vitest tests, all gates, smoke 433/433 and golden paths 23/23 (306/306 Playwright) clean throughout.

findings.title: Roughly 135 UI strings shipped this wave have no Arabic key
findings.detail: The four product agents added English source strings that fall back to English on an Arabic page: ~90 from inventory, ~31 from customers, 14 from workshop. t() never renders empty, so nothing is broken — but the Arabic UI shows English until the keys land in data/generated/ar.ts.
findings.why: Arabic and RTL are a first-class release target, not a late pass; the strings work the day they are translated.
findings.verified: reported with full string lists
findings.resolution: Stale — check-i18n.mjs now reports 3660/3660 unique literal t() keys covered (0 missing) across the whole app, confirmed clean in every gates run this session. The specific string lists these two findings named were translated in earlier waves; this closes them out formally since neither was ever marked fixed.

findings.title: No server collections for procurement — requisitions and purchase orders
findings.detail: server/src/registry.ts has no requisitions or purchase-orders collection, and no bespoke procurement router. Agent 11 built the requisition lifecycle and PurchaseOrder screen bounded to what the server supports and surfaced the rest as honest absent-capability states with GAP: tests. A requisition or PO cannot actually be persisted end to end yet.
findings.why: The procurement golden path (requisition → PO → receiving) cannot complete server-side. The UI is honest about it, but the capability is not real until the collections and approval-ceiling enforcement exist.
findings.verified: confirmed on a reset DB — 406 server tests, the ceiling and over-receipt invariants proven over HTTP
findings.resolution: Procurement backend built (migration 0010): a suppliers master, requisitions (+lines, submit/approve/reject) and purchase orders (+lines, raise-from-requisition, approve within ceiling with SOD, receive). The PO total is server-computed and cannot exceed the approvers ceiling (requireApproval); over-receipt is refused unless approval-gated; receiving is idempotent. Stock movement on receipt is deferred deliberately (a PO line part reference is optional free text). Client repository wired; agent 11 wires the screens next.

findings.title: The Inventory screen does not offer the return / adjust_down / reservation movements the server now enforces
findings.detail: F-017 added return, adjust_down and reservation endpoints and contract types, but Inventory.tsx's MOVEMENT_KINDS array and modal still describe the original five kinds. The server enforces the new movements; no UI raises them.
findings.why: The enforcement is real but partially unreachable from the product until the screen wires the two new kinds and a reservation control. Purely additive UI work.
findings.verified: confirmed on the quiet tree — inventory suite 82 green, gates at baseline
findings.resolution: Agent 10 wired all three into the Inventory modal: return books through its own delta (not receiving), adjust gained an explicit up/down (qty positive, type carries the sign), and reserve/release write parts.reserved with a 'draw from reservation' path on consume. Each kind has a test proving the UI maps the server's refusal to the right field; inventory-invariant.test.ts holds the On Hand equation across a sequence including the new kinds.

findings.title: Two procurement-portal screens still render AppShell instead of PortalShell
findings.detail: F-009's root cause is fixed (PortalShell exists), but /procurement-portal and /procurement-portal/requisitions are declared in the legacy app map and render AppShell. Migrating them needs a PortalShell SURFACES entry and a barrel declaration with shell: PortalShell.
findings.why: A registry shell-mismatch that the completion matrix will keep flagging until the migration lands. Cosmetic today; the screens work.
findings.verified: reported by agent 16 as the deferred integration step
findings.resolution: ProcurementPortal and ProcurementPortal.Requisitions are implemented in network/Procurement.tsx, not a screens/domains/ file portals.ts owns, so routes/index.tsx splits them out of APP_SCREENS into their own PROCUREMENT_PORTAL_SCREENS map, composed with shell: PortalShell (asDomain(..., PortalShell)) rather than adding a per-screen override to the shared asDomain helper. PortalShell.tsx's SURFACES table gained a real /procurement-portal entry (title, icon, Home + Requisitions nav, gated on the existing portalprocure module grants). build-registry.mjs's static analysis specifically looks for the named APP_SCREENS/CUSTOMER_APP_SCREENS/PUBLIC_SCREENS blocks to decide what's IMPLEMENTED vs DISCOVERED — splitting the two screens into a new block without teaching that script about it first regressed check-no-fake to 2 false placeholders; fixed by adding PROCUREMENT_PORTAL_SCREENS as a fourth recognized block, the same shape as the other three. 3941/3941 app tests (1 new, 1 rewritten so its own 'unregistered surface' example does not reuse a route that just became registered), tsc and all gates clean, smoke 433/433, golden paths 23/23.

findings.title: No public lead endpoint, so the marketing Contact form cannot submit
findings.detail: Nothing under server/ accepts an anonymous contact/lead POST. Agent 17's Contact form validates then shows a role=alert failure naming direct channels (mailto/tel); there is deliberately no success path. §A28 marketing analytics has no infrastructure either.
findings.why: A visitor cannot contact the business through the site. Surfaced honestly rather than faked, but the capability is absent.
findings.verified: confirmed — the route, its rate-limit registration, env defaults and no-escalation properties read directly by the orchestrator
findings.resolution: POST /public/leads, unauthenticated: a .strict() body with no orgId, a synthetic principal pinned to a configured PUBLIC_LEAD_ORG_ID so no other tenant is reachable, a per-IP rate limit (@fastify/rate-limit, default 5/min), a dedicated public_leads intake table, a 202 bare acknowledgement, and no PII in logs — the contact lives in the audit ledger for triage, never a log line. Agent 17s Contact form can now submit; wiring it is agent 17s follow-up.

findings.title: ~172 new UI strings across portals and the public site have no Arabic key
findings.detail: Agent 16 added ~47 and agent 17 ~125 English source strings that fall back to English on an Arabic page via t(). Nothing is broken; the Arabic UI shows English until the keys land in ar.ts. Full lists are in the two agents' reports.
findings.why: Arabic/RTL is a first-class release target; these surfaces are not Arabic-complete until the keys are added.
findings.verified: reported with full string lists
findings.resolution: Stale — check-i18n.mjs now reports 3660/3660 unique literal t() keys covered (0 missing) across the whole app, confirmed clean in every gates run this session. The specific string lists these two findings named were translated in earlier waves; this closes them out formally since neither was ever marked fixed.

findings.title: CRM and fleet collections are read-only, and several endpoints do not exist
findings.detail: Agent 09 built LeadDetail, CRMCalendar, CustomerFeedback and FleetContract but the backend cannot persist their writes: leads/opportunities/crmTasks/fleets are not writable; there is no lead→opportunity conversion route, no lead activity/notes collection, no feedback collection or POST /customer-feedback, and fleets carries no contract-term fields (type, value, dates, renewal) nor an exposed fleetId→vehicles join.
findings.why: Four rendered CRM surfaces are read/interactive only — honest, tested gap states rather than fake persistence, but the capabilities are not real until the collections and routes exist.
findings.verified: confirmed on a reset database — 292 server tests, app 697, gates at baseline
findings.resolution: leads/opportunities/crmTasks/fleets are writable through the generic router (RBAC, RLS, audit and optimistic concurrency come with it); customer_feedback table + collection + POST /customer-feedback; fleet contract terms on the schema + POST /fleets/:id/renew; lead→opportunity conversion in one transaction; and customers now present fleetId. findings.title: No financial aggregate endpoints, and four report-source collections are missing
findings.detail: Agent 12 refused to compute any cross-record money total in the browser (§A10: the server computes, the client displays) — and the server exposes none: no GET /invoices/summary, /accounting/tax/return, or trial-balance. SalesReports, TaxManagement and ReportsAnalytics therefore show only per-row server figures and disclose the absent totals. Also missing as collections: bankStatements (BankReconciliation has nothing to match), savedReports (CustomReports cannot persist a definition), insuranceClaims and loanContracts (Insurance/Loan reports have no data source).
findings.why: The reporting surfaces are built and honest but cannot show a real total or reconcile until the server computes aggregates. This is the §A10 discipline working as intended — the gap is server-side.
findings.verified: confirmed on a reset database — 312 server tests, app 697, gates at baseline; the aggregate numbers and tenant-isolation both pinned
findings.resolution: Three server-computed aggregate endpoints (§A10 — every total summed in SQL inside the RLS transaction, never handed to the client): GET /invoices/summary (invoiced/paid/outstanding/VAT with a byStatus breakdown), GET /accounting/tax/return (output VAT at the configurable VAT_RATE_BPS, input VAT declared not-modelled rather than faked), and GET /accounting/reports/trial-balance — which surfaces F-008 honestly: assets 2,683,500 vs liabilities+equity 2,940,550, differenceHalalas -25,705,000, balanced:false, the books not forced to tie. Plus bankStatements (with an idempotent audited POST /bank-statements/:id/match) and savedReports collections, migration 0005, both RLS-scoped. Client repository wired with a typed financeReports accessor. insuranceClaims/loanContracts were deliberately deferred to the greenfield insurance/loans schema rather than stubbed. Screen wiring (SalesReports, TaxManagement, ReportsAnalytics, BankReconciliation, CustomReports) is agent 12s follow-up — the AGGREGATE_GAP endpoint strings already match the paths shipped.

findings.title: Workshop approval and diagnostics surfaces exceed what the server exposes
findings.detail: Agent 08 built nine screens; several need server capabilities that do not exist: no unified GET /approvals (ApprovalInbox operates on estimates alone); estimates present() omits submittedBy and there is no GET /estimates/:id/history or /jobs/:id/history, so the SOD conflict cannot be flagged per row (the F-004 client half); estimates present() omits subtotalHalalas/taxHalalas though the schema has them, so no VAT breakdown; no server-computed diagnostic-report total; no GET /reports/workshop analytics; no OBD device commands or per-device DTC readings; no approval OTP/e-signature persistence and no approvalLines→estimate link.
findings.why: The screens render real data and defer honestly where the server is silent, but the approvals/diagnostics capabilities are partial until these endpoints exist.
findings.verified: confirmed on a reset database — 342 server tests, app 697, gates at baseline; each endpoint pinned by a numbers test and a tenant-isolation test
findings.resolution: Five endpoints, all server-computed and tenant-scoped: estimate present() exposes subtotal/tax/discount + submittedBy/approvedBy; GET /estimates/:id/history and /jobs/:id/history return the audit trail with SOD activities annotated and conflicts named — closing the F-004 client half, tenant-scoped twice (record resolution under RLS + audit_log RLS) and permission-gated; a unified GET /approvals whose rows carry canApprove/withinCeiling/isSubmitter so the inbox and engine cannot disagree; GET /reports/workshop with QC pass rate, bay time and technician hours summed in SQL, plus the server diagnostic total. OBD device commands and approval OTP ship as adapter-plus-mock (§40) refusing with a 503 external_dependency_unavailable that names the OBD bridge / SMS provider — never faked live; the obd_dtc_readings device↔dtc link is real persisted data (migration 0006). approvalLines→estimate FK deferred as gold-plating (no consumer this tranche). Screen wiring is agent 08s follow-up.

findings.title: Seed appointments do not reconcile with the technician roster
findings.detail: app/src/data/generated/tables.ts: APPOINTMENTS[].tech names (Saeed Al-Zahrani, Majed Al-Otaibi, Yousef Al-Ghamdi) are not in TECHS (Yousef Al-Otaibi, Bandar Al-Qahtani, Faisal Al-Harbi, Nasser Al-Dosari), and there is no technicianId link. Grouping a schedule on the roster alone shows every technician idle.

findings.title: Four Tier C public pages have no registry route to build against
findings.detail: Agent 17 built Privacy and Terms, but Pricing, Request/Book Demo, Careers and Cookie Policy do not exist in the generated screen registry, and AppRoutes only renders registry entries. A website agent cannot add them from within its boundary — the screen names/routes must be added to the generator source first.

findings.verified: reported by agent 17
findings.resolution: Pricing, Book/Request Demo, Careers and Cookie Policy all carry real SCREEN_MAP.md routes and render live today (confirmed while investigating BLK-010/F-037) — this finding predates that fix and was never closed out. The generator/registry gap it described no longer exists.

findings.title: external_dependency_unavailable is not in the client RepositoryErrorCode union
findings.detail: The server sends error code external_dependency_unavailable with status 503 for an unconfigured integration (OBD bridge, SMS). repository.ts's RepositoryErrorCode union does not list it, so agent 08's handler keys on the 503 status and casts the code. Works at runtime; the string is untyped.
findings.why: A minor type gap: the honest EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY handling works, but the code is not in the shared taxonomy the client types against.
findings.verified: reported by agent 08
findings.resolution: external_dependency_unavailable added to repository.ts's RepositoryErrorCode union, matching packages/contract's real ErrorCode. workshop/api.ts's isExternalDependency dropped the `error.code as string` cast it used to compare against the literal outside the union — the 503-status check next to it was already sufficient at runtime, so behaviour is unchanged; only the type gap is closed. tsc and all gates clean.

findings.title: Feature-map screens with no SCREEN_MODULE mapping open for any role, then 403 on their data
findings.detail: Insurance-Claims (and other feature-map screens absent from the design bundle's SCREEN_MODULE) has no module mapping, so canScreen returns true and any authenticated role opens the workspace — but its collections are gated server-side, so every fetch 403s into an ErrorState. The data is safe; the defect is UX.
findings.why: Not a security hole — the boundary holds — but a screen that opens then errors reads as broken. Fix: give feature-map screens a SCREEN_MODULE entry so nav and data agree.
findings.verified: reported by agent 13
findings.resolution: 17 feature-map/portal screens were cross-referenced against every useCollection/useQuery call site and the server registry's module grants to find every case where the missing SCREEN_MODULE entry was not just cosmetic (most of the ~200 unmapped feature-map screens render only static FEATURE_DEFS content, so they never fetch and never 403). project/gms-data.js's SCREEN_MODULE now maps: Insurance-Claims, Payroll-Management, Timesheet-Management, Timeclock-Payroll and Leave-Requests to "hr"; Interactive-3D-Parts to "inventory"; Purchase-Agent-Payments and Purchase-Agent-Suppliers to "procurement"; Client-Portal-Appointments to "appointments"; Client-Portal-Vehicles to "vehicles"; Technician-App-Jobs, Technician-Mobile, Technician-Portal-Dashboard, Technician-Portal-My-Jobs and Workshop-Calendar to "jobcards"; Email-Marketing-Campaigns to "crm"; and Customers-List to "customers" — all verified against real role grants in gms-data.js's PERMS (tests/rbac-matrix.test.ts already asserts every SCREEN_MODULE value is a valid module with at least one viewing role, and now covers these 17). One related screen, Staff-Directory / HR-Management, was investigated and deliberately left out of this fix — tracked as F-038, since mapping it to "hr" would newly 403 the HR role on its own directory. 3938/3938 app tests (incl. 2336 rbac-matrix assertions), rbac-parity clean, tsc and all gates clean, smoke 433/433, golden paths 23/23.

findings.title: No real insurance or loans module in the RBAC matrix
findings.detail: Insurance/loans collections and the claim lifecycle are gated on `accounting` (the matrix has no insurance/loans module). accounting conflates ledger authority with claim adjudication. A dedicated insurance/loans module with its own approve column and ceiling would model the real segregation.
findings.why: Workable proxy today; a real module is a one-line re-point per collection once the matrix carries it.
findings.verified: reported by both agents
findings.resolution: Insurance policies/claims and loan contracts/repayments (4 collections) and the insurance-claim lifecycle (submit/approve/reject/pay) were gated on the module 'accounting', so an accountant's ledger authority and their claim-adjudication authority were the same permission cell — the exact conflation the finding named. No dedicated insurance/loans role exists in the 15-role roster to receive different grants, so a full RBAC redesign was out of scope; the buildable, real fix is the one the finding's own 'why' field anticipated: split a dedicated 'insurance' module into the matrix with the current 'accounting' cells copied onto it verbatim (owner 'vax', manager 'vx', accountant 'vcedax', superadmin 'v', test 'vcedax' — every other role unchanged at ''), so ledger and claim-adjudication authority can diverge later without a re-point touching general accounting access. 'Its own approve column' is achieved (insurance:a is now a distinct cell, not accounting:a); 'its own ceiling' already exists independent of any module — approvalCeilingHalalas is per-role in ROLE_META and requireApproval already enforces it against the approved amount, same as every other approval path (estimates, requisitions, purchase orders) — a module never carried its own ceiling anywhere in this codebase, so there was nothing insurance-specific to add there. Re-pointed: packages/contract/src/rbac.ts (moduleId enum + PERMS row) and project/gms-data.js (mirrored), the 4 collection definitions in server/src/registry.ts, the bespoke server/src/routes/insurance-claims.ts (CLAIM_MODULE), server/src/routes/approvals.ts's insuranceClaimItems (the unified approval queue now reports insurance claims under module 'insurance'), server/src/routes/product-reports.ts's two report endpoints (insurance/claims/summary, loans/summary), and SCREEN_MODULE's Insurance-Claims entry (accounting -> insurance). tools/docs/lib/model.mjs's CAP-ACCOUNTING capability gained 'insurance' in its module list so the doc generator's capability map still covers these four collections' endpoints. Regenerated app/src/data/generated/rbac.ts. A 32nd module broke the same class of hardcoded module-count assertions F-038 already hit (app/tests/rbac-matrix.test.ts's ALL_MODULES array and count, app/tests/unit/rbac.test.ts's count) — fixed the same way, by adding 'insurance' to the explicit list and bumping the literal counts (the other four assertions this class affects were already made to derive from .length during F-038 and needed no further change). Updated test comments and one literal module-name assertion in server/tests/approvals-queue.test.ts and server/tests/insurance-loans.test.ts that named 'accounting' where the grants and behavior are unchanged (same role, same outcome) but the module name itself is now 'insurance'. tsc clean in app/ and server/, 4091/4091 app vitest tests, 558/558 server vitest tests, all gates, smoke 433/433, golden paths 23/23 (306/306 Playwright), docs generate/check clean.

findings.title: InsuranceReports/LoanReports still render the stale gap though their data now exists
findings.detail: GapReports.tsx (agent 12's boundary) still shows 'no data source yet' for insuranceClaims/loanContracts, but those collections and the productReports aggregates now exist. The two reports should graduate against them.
findings.why: A small wiring follow-up: F-028 deferred these to the greenfield schema, which has now landed.
findings.verified: fixed by the orchestrator; app 813 tests, gates at baseline
findings.resolution: InsuranceReports and LoanReports read productReports.insuranceClaimsSummary/loansSummary on the live path and keep the honest gap on the fixture build. No client-side aggregate.

findings.title: Three generated files (nav.ts, rbac.ts, badges.ts) were hand-patched past what the generator now produces, so a routine `npm run port-design` silently reverts real fixes
findings.detail: Running port-design-data.mjs to fix F-008/F-010 also (a) dropped ~9 real AI/automation and voice nav entries from NAV that exist as routed screens in app/src but were never added to handoff/SCREEN_MAP.md, and (b) reverted rbac.ts's and badges.ts's role/status colors from theme-aware CSS custom properties (`var(--salis-blue)`, `var(--tint-orange)`, etc. — needed for dark-mode support) back to hardcoded hex/rgba literals, because whoever added dark-mode theming patched the generated output directly instead of the generator's color-emission logic or its design-bundle source. Caught before committing by diffing every regenerated file rather than trusting `npm run gates` alone (gates don't check for a theming regression). nav.ts, rbac.ts and badges.ts were reverted to their pre-regeneration content this pass; only screens.ts (2 legitimate SCREEN_MAP.md rows added: PublicPortal.RoiCalculator, PublicPortal.Security — themselves a smaller instance of the same problem) and tables.ts (F-008's balance fix) were kept from the regeneration.
findings.why: The repo's stated contract is 'generated files are never edited by hand — the generator is the only writer.' That contract has been broken at least twice (nav/colors, and the two public-site screens) without anyone re-running the generator to notice, so the generator now actively fights recent real fixes instead of reproducing them. The next person who runs `npm run port-design` for an unrelated reason will hit the same silent regression unless this is fixed at the generator/source level.
findings.verified: confirmed by diffing every file port-design-data.mjs rewrote against HEAD before committing; reverted the two destructive files, kept the two safe ones, all tests/gates/build still pass
findings.resolution: project/gms-data.js's ROLES colors and SVC_BADGE/ST_BADGE/PR_BADGE tint/color pairs were rewritten from literal hex/rgba to the CSS custom properties (var(--salis-blue), var(--tint-orange), etc.) the hand-patch had added for dark-mode support — 10 mappings, ~41 occurrences. The 10 screens missing from NAV/SCREEN_MAP.md/SCREEN_MODULE (DeclinedJobs and 9 AI/voice screens) were added to project/handoff/SCREEN_MAP.md and gms-data.js's NAV/SCREEN_MODULE, using the hyphenated screen names ("AI-Automation", "Voice-Commands", etc.) that RequireAccess actually checks for spec-screen-routed screens — the PascalCase form the original hand-patch (and this fix's first draft) used was a dead SCREEN_MODULE key, which meant those 9 screens, including the 2 already shipped (Voice-Commands, Voice-Command-Interface), were reachable by every role regardless of the "ai" module grant. `node scripts/port-design-data.mjs` now reproduces nav.ts/rbac.ts/badges.ts byte-for-byte against what previously required a hand-patch (0 git diff on badges.ts/ar.ts/tables.ts after regeneration). 3914/3914 app tests, 554/554 server tests (incl. rbac-parity.test.ts), tsc and all gates clean.

findings.title: Ten public-website screen files were unreachable from any route (BLK-010)
findings.detail: The "SALIS AUTO 2030" design study shipped a six-page tour (Arrival, System, Grid, Access, Origin, Channel) plus its own nav shell (PageNav, CommandDeck) — complete, working React, never linked into the site. Landing.tsx's 2026-09-16 rewrite superseded Arrival with a new homepage and explicitly deferred the other five as "a later cascade-phase task".
findings.why: BLK-010 in project-control/BLOCKERS.json flagged all 10 files as orphaned. Real, already-written product content (domain architecture, supply chain, plan comparison, company story, onboarding) sitting dead in the repo.
findings.verified: fixed and tested this session
findings.resolution: The five content pages were rewritten onto the site's light-first design system (matching Pricing/Features/About) and given real routes: PublicPortal.Platform (/public-portal/platform), .SupplyChain (/public-portal/supply-chain), .ComparePlans (/public-portal/compare-plans), .CompanyStory (/public-portal/story) and .GettingStarted (/public-portal/getting-started) — wired into SCREEN_MAP.md, the website.ts barrel, sitemap.xml and the Footer, with cross-links from About.tsx and Pricing.tsx. One material correction made along the way: the study's Access page published a numeric plan-comparison matrix (branch/user ceilings, SLA hours, uptime percentages) and a "Starter" plan name found nowhere else in the codebase, contradicting Pricing.tsx's deliberate no-published-numbers policy, and one FAQ answer's blanket data-export promise contradicted the already-shipped Security.tsx. ComparePlans.tsx and CompanyStory.tsx use Pricing.tsx's real plan names and keep every differentiation qualitative — see those files' docstrings. The old six-page tour's dead scaffolding (CommandDeck.tsx, PageNav.tsx, IndexPage.tsx, landing.css, useLandingMotion.ts) was deleted; types.ts and landingData.ts were trimmed to their still-live exports. BLK-010 now lists one file — SocialProofBand.tsx — which is a deliberate, documented reservation for future testimonials, not orphaned debt.

findings.title: Staff-Directory / HR-Management reads a collection gated to a narrower module than the screen itself
findings.detail: app/src/screens/hr/StaffDirectory.tsx (screens Staff-Directory and HR-Management) calls useCollection('departments'), whose server route is registered with module:'admin' (server/src/registry.ts:502) — owner/manager/superadmin/test only. The natural SCREEN_MODULE mapping is "hr", but that would leave the HR role itself 403ing on its own staff directory, since the hr role has no admin grant.
findings.why: Found while fixing F-033's broader SCREEN_MODULE gap. Deliberately not folded into that fix: it needs either module:'admin' on the screen (locks out HR staff, the wrong answer) or the departments collection's own module corrected from 'admin' to 'hr' server-side (a bigger, separate change with its own blast radius on Branches/admin-facing department management, outside a client-only SCREEN_MODULE fix).
findings.verified: reported this session, not yet fixed
findings.resolution: The departments collection was gated to module:'admin' server-side (server/src/registry.ts), while Staff-Directory/HR-Management/Departments are all mapped to the 'hr' SCREEN_MODULE — so any role with an 'hr' grant but no 'admin' grant (hr itself, and accountant, who also holds an 'hr' cell) would 403 reading the collection their own screen shows. Re-pointing the collection straight to module:'hr' (the fix this finding's own text floated and rejected) would have been a regression: 'hr' module's superadmin cell is view-only ('v') versus 'admin''s full 'vcedax', and folding department reads into the wide 'admin' module for hr/accountant would have also opened Branches/Users & Teams/Integrations/Templates to them — none of which are an HR concern. Fixed with a new dedicated module, 'departments', split off from 'admin' (packages/contract/src/rbac.ts's moduleId enum and PERMS, mirrored in project/gms-data.js, server/src/registry.ts's departments collection re-pointed to it): owner/superadmin/test keep exactly the 'vcedax'/'vcedax'/'vcedax' they had under 'admin', manager keeps its view-only 'v', and hr gains 'vc' (view, plus create — Accounting.tsx's Departments screen already shows HR an "Add Department" button on the strength of its own hr:'c' grant, which would otherwise still 403 on click) and accountant gains 'v' (matching the nav visibility 'hr' already grants it). SCREEN_MODULE gained Staff-Directory/HR-Management -> 'hr' (Departments was already mapped there). Regenerated app/src/data/generated/rbac.ts via npm run port-design. Adding a 31st module broke four hardcoded module-count assertions across server/tests/authz-matrix.test.ts, server/tests/auth-test-account.test.ts, app/tests/rbac-matrix.test.ts and app/tests/unit/rbac.test.ts (all pinned to the old count of 30/450/2700/2250) — fixed by deriving each from MODULE_IDS.length/ROLE_IDS.length/GRANT_ACTIONS.length instead of a literal, so the next module addition doesn't repeat this. tsc clean in both app/ and server/, 4016/4016 app vitest tests, 554/554 server vitest tests (incl. rbac-parity, authz-matrix, rbac-lab, auth-test-account), all gates, smoke 433/433, golden paths 23/23 (306/306 Playwright).

findings.title: The departments collection has no write routes at all — Add Department 404s for every role
findings.detail: server/src/registry.ts's departments define() block carries no `writable: true` (unlike collections such as branches or suppliers that do), and server/src/routes/collections.ts:182 only registers create/update/delete routes when `def.writable` is set (`const writer = def.writable ? WRITERS[def.key] : undefined`). So POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/departments do not exist on a live server at all — app/src/screens/accounting/DepartmentFormModal.tsx's useCreate('departments') call 404s for every role, including owner and superadmin, not just a permissions gap.
findings.why: Found while fixing F-038 (server/src/routes/collections.ts:182, tools/docs/generators/api.mjs's per-collection 'Writable' column, both keyed off the same `writable` flag). Out of scope there: F-038 is about read 403s on an existing route; this is a missing route, unrelated to which module gates it, and touching WRITERS['departments'] plus verifying the create/update/delete handlers is a separate, server-side change with its own test surface.
findings.verified: reported this session, not yet fixed
findings.resolution: The departments collection had no writer registered at all: no `writable: true` on its registry.ts definition, and no packages/contract entity/create/update schema (unlike every other writable collection). DepartmentFormModal's own inline schema also sent `code`/`manager` — field names that matched no column on either side (the real columns are `costCenter`/`head`), so a submission would have 400'd on an unknown field even once the route existed. Fixed for real, not just flagged: added packages/contract/src/entities/department.ts (departmentCreate/departmentUpdate, mirroring the fleets/suppliers convention — name required, head/costCenter/branchLabel/icon optional, headcount defaults to 0 since nothing links an employee row to a department id yet, so there is no real count to derive it from); registered it in server/src/writers.ts as a passthrough writer; set writable: true on the departments collection definition, which is what actually turns on POST/PATCH/DELETE/bulk-* route registration in routes/collections.ts's generic router (`if (!writer) return`). Fixed DepartmentFormModal.tsx to send `head`/`costCenter` instead of the two names that matched nothing, piped through the new contract schema instead of an inline one. New server/tests/departments-write.test.ts (4 tests) proves it end to end against the real API: hr can create (headcount defaults to 0), the create is audited, manager and accountant (view-only on the F-038 'departments' module) are refused with 403, and owner can edit/delete while hr (create-only, 'vc') is refused the edit — the RBAC split from F-038 holds exactly at the write boundary it was designed for. tsc clean in app/ and server/, 4016/4016 app vitest tests, 558/558 server vitest tests (554 existing + 4 new), all gates, smoke 433/433, golden paths 23/23, docs generate/check clean.

findings.title: AuditLog (D-AuditLog) rendered its hardcoded fixture rows even when isLive — one of BLK-004's 280 mock-only capabilities
findings.detail: app/src/screens/admin/AuditLog.tsx's `isLive` branch existed only to swap an empty-state gap notice for the real screen; once past that check, the component filtered the same module-level `FIXTURE_ENTRIES` constant regardless of `isLive`, so a live deployment showed the identical eight fabricated rows ("Khalid Al-Amri logged in", etc.) a fixture build did. No server endpoint backed it either — server/src/routes/history.ts only answers `GET /:collection/:id/history`, one entity's trail, never a flat cross-entity feed — so there was nothing for the screen to call even if it had tried.
findings.why: Directed by the user to wire up one of BLK-004's mock-only capabilities to the live API. AuditLog was chosen because the underlying data (`audit_log`, append-only, already written on every mutation by audit/audit.ts) already exists and is already read elsewhere (history.ts, security/sod.ts) — the gap was purely the missing org-wide feed endpoint and the screen's dead live branch, not a missing capability end to end.
findings.verified: fixed and tested this session
findings.resolution: Added server/src/routes/audit-log.ts: `GET /audit-log`, gated on the existing `audit:v` grant, reading `audit_log` left-joined to `users` (for the actor's display name) inside the caller's `withTenant` transaction, so it is tenant-scoped by the same RLS every other read relies on. `category` (auth/data/system) is derived, not stored — a `session`/`password_reset` entity is auth, a row with no human actor or written by something other than a live request (`source !== 'api'`) is system, everything else is data — and the SQL `?category=` filter is built from the identical partition so the two cannot drift apart. `?q=` searches action/entity/reason/actor-name with the same `%`/`_` ilike-escaping convention query.ts's collection search already uses. Registered in server/src/app.ts alongside the other bespoke read routers. app/src/data/repository.ts gained `AuditLogApi`/`createAuditLogApi`/`auditLogApi`, following the existing `history`/`productReports`/`financeReports` convention exactly: live-only, null on a fixture build, no mock implementation, because a cross-entity audit trail is a server computation a fixture cannot honestly reproduce. AuditLog.tsx was rewritten to fetch through `useQuery` + `auditLogApi`, deriving its icon/verb/category styling from the entry's real `action`/`entity`/`category` fields (a `session`+`create` row reads "logged in", a `password_reset` row reads "requested a password reset", everything else reads as its own action verb plus entity name) instead of the fixture's per-row hand-authored strings; the always-hardcoded `FIXTURE_ENTRIES` array is gone, and the decorative "Load more" button (never wired to any pagination cursor, mock or real) was removed rather than kept as a second dead control. New server/tests/audit-log-read.test.ts (7 tests) proves it against the real API: a role without `audit:v` gets 403; another organization's rows never appear; the actor-name join resolves a real seeded user; all three category buckets are assigned correctly on rows constructed to hit each one; `?category=auth` narrows correctly; `?q=` finds a row by its `reason`; `?limit=` caps the page. tsc clean in app/ and server/, 4091/4091 app vitest tests, 565/565 server vitest tests (558 existing + 7 new). See F-041 for a measurement gap this surfaced: the registry's automated `dataBacked`/MOCK_ONLY heuristic does not recognize this kind of bespoke live-only API call, so `npm run registry` still counts D-AuditLog (and, pre-existing, D-InsuranceReports/D-LoanReports) as mock-only despite being genuinely live and tested.

findings.title: build-registry.mjs's dataBacked/MOCK_ONLY heuristic only recognizes the generic useCollection/useEntity/useCreate/useUpdate/useDelete/useBulk seam — every screen wired through a bespoke live-only API object is still counted mock-only
findings.detail: app/scripts/build-registry.mjs's `dataBackedScreens` map is built by matching `SEAM_CALL` — `use(PagedCollection|Collection|Entity|Create|Update|Delete|Bulk)('literal-key')` — against each screen's exported source. That is the only thing `dataBacked` (and therefore the `MOCK_ONLY` flag and BLK-004's headline count) measures. A screen that instead reads through one of the bespoke, live-only API accessors repository.ts exports at its own bottom — `financeReports`, `productReports`, `history`, `approvals`, `workshopReports`, `diagnostics`, `estimateOtp`, `insuranceClaimsApi`, `procurement`, and now `auditLogApi` (F-040) — calls no seam hook with a literal collection string, so the regex never sees it and the screen is flagged MOCK_ONLY regardless of whether it is genuinely live.
findings.why: Found confirming F-040's fix: `npm run registry` left D-AuditLog's `dataBacked` at `false` and BLK-004's count unchanged after AuditLog was wired to a real, tested endpoint, which looked at first like the fix had not registered. Checking MASTER_REGISTRY.json showed D-InsuranceReports and D-LoanReports — both already wired to server/src/routes/product-reports.ts before this session, unrelated to F-040 — carry the identical false MOCK_ONLY flag today, confirming this is a pre-existing blind spot in the measurement script, not something F-040 introduced or could have avoided by wiring AuditLog differently.
findings.verified: fixed and verified this session
findings.resolution: app/scripts/build-registry.mjs now recognises the bespoke live-only accessors, derived from app/src/data/repository.ts rather than listed in the script, so this measurement cannot go stale the way this finding describes. The accessors are found by the declaration shape they share — `export const X: XApi | null = API_URL ? createXApi(API_URL) : null` — which picks up all eleven of them (httpRepository, financeReports, history, auditLogApi, approvals, workshopReports, diagnostics, estimateOtp, insuranceClaimsApi, productReports, procurement) and will pick up a twelfth with no edit. Each factory is then read method by method for the endpoint that method requests, including through a local URL helper such as createDiagnosticsApi's `device()`, so `approvals.list()` records `approvals` and `diagnostics.integrations()` records `diagnostics/integrations`: dataSource says what the screen is backed by, not merely that it is. A screen is credited only for a method call on an accessor it imports from that module — seventeen screen files carry the words "approvals" or "diagnostics" in prose or UI copy and one keeps a local `diagnostics` parts basket, and none of them are credited — and a screen that imports an accessor only to null-check it and render the honest gap notice (accounting/GapReports) makes no call and keeps its flag. Measured on base bac4f4e: D-AuditLog is the one capability this clears, because it is the only one whose sole backing was a bespoke accessor; seven screens that were already data-backed through the collection seam gain the bespoke endpoint they were silently omitting (ApprovalInbox +approvals, CustomerApproval +estimates/:id/request-approval-otp +.../verify-approval-otp, EstimateDetail +estimates/:id/history, OBDDiagnostics +diagnostics/integrations +diagnostics/devices/:id/readings, WorkshopQC +jobs/:id/history, WorkshopReports +reports/workshop, Insurance-Claims +insurance/claims/summary), which was the same defect in a quieter form. D-InsuranceReports and D-LoanReports, named in this finding, were already cleared by the REPORT_HOOK detector added since it was written. Not addressed here and still open as a measurement question: dataBacked/dataSource are read from a screen's own file only, while the CRUD pass follows cross-file mounts — on this base no MOCK_ONLY screen is reached by that pass, so it moves no rows today.

findings.title: Profile's "Save Changes" always showed success without calling the server — name and password edits were entirely fake
findings.detail: app/src/screens/admin/Profile.tsx's `handleSave` never called any API: on a live build it validated the password fields client-side (with the wrong minimum — `MIN_PW = 8` where the server's `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` is 12, so a password the form accepted would have 401'd had a real call ever been made) and then unconditionally showed a "Profile updated" toast, cleared the fields, and returned. Neither the display name nor the password ever reached `users.name` or `users.password_hash`. No endpoint existed for either action: `GET /auth/me` was read-only, and `resetPassword`/`setPassword` are the token-carried recovery flow and the administrative-provisioning path respectively, not a signed-in caller changing a password they already know.
findings.why: Found while picking the next BLK-004 mock-only capability after F-040 (AuditLog). D-Profile's MASTER_REGISTRY.json entry carries `MOCK_ONLY`; unlike D-UsersTeams (whose Users table, `admin/staff`, was already live and only its Teams section was genuinely unwired to a nonexistent `teams` concept — a schema decision, not a wiring gap) and D-RolesPermissions (an RBAC-matrix editor with no server-side mutable-permissions concept at all — also a schema/product decision), Profile's data already exists in full (`users.name`, `users.password_hash`) and only the two routes and the client call were missing, making it the clean, scoped candidate.
findings.verified: fixed and tested this session
findings.resolution: Added `PATCH /auth/me` (updates the caller's own `name`; nothing else on the row is reachable this way) and `POST /auth/change-password` (verifies the current password with `verifyPassword` before accepting a new one, and revokes every session — including the caller's own refresh token — the same invariant `resetPassword` already holds the codebase to, per the module's own stated properties in `auth/service.ts`'s docstring) to `server/src/auth/{service,routes}.ts`, following the file's existing conventions exactly (zod body schemas beside the other auth bodies, `AuthFailure` for a wrong current password so it maps to 401 like every other credential failure, `writeAudit` on both actions). `SessionProvider.tsx` gained `updateProfile`/`changePassword`, implemented with the same `authFetch` helper `switchRole`/`revokeDevice` already use; a successful name change calls `setUser` so the sidebar and avatar reflect it immediately, with no extra `/auth/me` round trip. Profile.tsx now calls both through `useSession()` when `live`, surfaces a real error (wrong current password, unmet policy, network) via toast instead of a blanket success, and disables the button while the request is in flight; non-live (demo/fixture) builds keep the original local-only toast, since there is no server row to write. Also fixed the pre-existing client/server password-length mismatch while touching this code: `MIN_PW = 8` was silently wrong against the server's `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 12` (the value the invite-acceptance, registration and reset-password forms already hardcode with an identical comment) — a password the form accepted would have been refused by the very endpoint this fix wires up. New `server/tests/auth-profile.test.ts` (9 tests) proves both endpoints end to end: a name update is visible on the next `GET /auth/me`; an empty name 400s; no token 401s; a wrong current password 401s and leaves the real password usable; a correct change works and the old password stops working; every session (including the refresh token used to sign in) is revoked by a change; a policy-violating new password 401s with the server's own message. tsc clean in app/ and server/, 4160/4160 app vitest tests, 726/726 server vitest tests (717 existing + 9 new), all gates (including check-i18n, after adding the two new Arabic strings and the corrected password-length copy), docs generate/check clean, smoke 436/436, golden paths 23/23 (306/306 Playwright).

findings.title: KioskCheckIn's service picker offered six invented services with no server counterpart, instead of the real `services` catalog every other booking screen already reads
findings.detail: app/src/screens/portals/KioskCheckIn.tsx hardcoded `FIXTURE_SERVICES` — six `{id, label, icon}` entries ("Oil Change", "Tire Rotation", "Brake Inspection", "Full Service", "AC Service", "Battery Check") with no server-side counterpart — and rendered it unconditionally, live build or not. The `serviceLabel` on the appointment it files therefore never named a real catalog entry: `server/src/db/schema.ts`'s `services` table (a per-tenant `{icon, label}` list, already registered as the read-only `services` collection in `server/src/registry.ts`, gated on `jobcards:v`) was sitting unused by this screen despite `CustomerPortalBooking.tsx` already reading it through `useCollection('services')` for the identical picker.
findings.why: Found scanning for the same antipattern F-040 (AuditLog) and F-042 (Profile) fixed — a screen-local `FIXTURE_` constant rendered regardless of `isLive` — after the registry's MOCK_ONLY-tagged candidates ran out of ones that were both genuinely unwired and did not require a new schema concept (D-UsersTeams' Teams section and D-RolesPermissions both need one; D-HealthCheckReport and D-Profile were false positives already backed by real endpoints the registry's heuristic doesn't recognise). `grep`ing for `FIXTURE_` + `isLive` co-occurring in the same screen file surfaced this one directly: real backing data existed and only the client was pointed at a fabricated list instead of it.
findings.verified: fixed and tested this session
findings.resolution: Rewired KioskCheckIn.tsx onto `useCollection('services')`, following CustomerPortalBooking's own established pattern exactly: `services.data` presents as `[icon, label]` tuples (the collection is read-only and carries no row id, per its `registry.ts` definition), so the label itself is now the selection value in place of the fixture's invented `id`, and `handleConfirm`'s `serviceLabel` is `selectedService` directly rather than a lookup into the deleted fixture array. `ServiceStep` gained loading/error props (`Loading`/`ErrorState`, matching the booking screen's own handling) instead of always rendering a populated list. This also fixed the demo/fixture build, not only the live one: the mock repository's `services` collection is backed by the same `T.SERVICES` fixture table (`Maintenance`, `Repair`, `Diagnostics`, ...) every other service picker in the app already shows, so a walk-in at a demo terminal now sees the same catalog a customer booking online does, not a screen-specific invented one. Updated `app/tests/kiosk-identify.test.tsx`'s three `Oil Change` button-role queries to the real fixture's first entry, `Maintenance`, and added an assertion that the filed appointment's `serviceLabel` is exactly that value. `npm run registry` now credits this screen for real — `dataBacked: true`, `dataSource: ['appointments', 'services']`, `MOCK_ONLY` gone — because `useCollection` is the seam the heuristic was already built to recognise, unlike F-040/F-042's bespoke-accessor and provider-method cases. tsc clean in app/, 4160/4160 app vitest tests (10/10 in the updated file), all gates, docs generate/check clean.
